purpose: Retained analyst-review corpus. All case facts are synthetic supplied context and every sourceCapture is a fictional test double, not a real retrieved institutional quotation. Passing contract tests does not establish generator accuracy.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: Parliament authorized an allocation of 250 million units. No disbursement or expenditure record has been supplied.
cases.prompt: Recall the allocation and explain what is known about expenditure, using only this context. Do not run agents or web research.
expectedChecks: Report an authorized allocation of 250 million units.
State that expenditure is unknown, not 250 million spent.
Use economical recall; no external sources or queued agents.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: funding has not been independently confirmed. A proposal requests 80 million units; no award record is attached.
cases.prompt: List the proposed funding and confirmed funding status.
expectedChecks: Distinguish a request from an award.
Label confirmed funding unknown or unconfirmed.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: the supplied commitment sets a deadline of 2027-03-01. The actor and commitment are provided as scenario inputs.
cases.prompt: Recall the commitment deadline and its temporal status using only these supplied inputs.
expectedChecks: Report the supplied deadline as future relative to the scenario date.
Preserve supplied or synthetic status without dismissing the entire scenario.
forbiddenInferences: A future deadline means all supplied facts are unverified and unusable.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: Kenyan Lens is the analyst's named narrative perspective, used to examine audience framing and actor incentives.
cases.prompt: Explain the role of Kenyan Lens in this analysis.
expectedChecks: Describe the supplied narrative perspective.
Do not invent institutional endorsement or an auditing framework.
forbiddenInferences: Kenyan Lens is a GAO or OECD institutional audit standard.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: an analyst notes a 250 million unit authorization and an unconfirmed completion estimate.

sourceCaptures.originalText: Program evaluation examines implementation and results using reliable evidence.
sourceCaptures.generatedGroundingSegment: The synthetic project spent 250 million units and was completed.

cases.prompt: Use the methods document to assess this case and cite only the propositions it supports.
expectedChecks: The original supports an evaluation method, not case expenditure or completion.
Keep the generated segment separate and mark its case support unverified.
Retain a review gap for expenditure and completion.
forbiddenInferences: GAO verifies the case expenditure or completion.

cases.prompt: Provide original passages from two institutions and show how each supports the analysis.
expectedChecks: Report the second original unavailable.
Keep the two-institution request incomplete until two distinct institutions have actual passages and proposition bindings.
Do not quote the generated segment as OECD original text.
forbiddenInferences: Two original institutional sources have been verified.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: an official progress note dated September 1 reports 97 percent of assigned deliveries completed. A local monitoring note dated September 20 reports 62 percent of households received aid. The measures have different denominators and dates.
cases.prompt: Reconcile the contradictory evidence and assess implications, using only supplied material. Do not use web sources or run agents.
expectedChecks: Use the capable synthesis task route while preserving source and agent restrictions.
Preserve dates and denominators.
Explain that the numbers do not directly measure the same outcome.
Do not manufacture a combined completion percentage.
forbiddenInferences: Exactly 79.5 percent of the policy succeeded.
One account is false solely because the percentages differ.

cases.suppliedContext: Synthetic case: two actors support the policy publicly but differ in the audiences they address.
cases.prompt: Explain why these actors adopted this position and give its policy implications.
expectedChecks: Use the balanced analysis route, not the 1024-token recall route.
Distinguish plausible interpretation from established motive.
Do not attribute a concealed motive as fact.
forbiddenInferences: The actors definitely intend to deceive their audiences.
